windows.reason: Windows gate approved with waiver: the ROCm/HIP port is functional on Windows gfx1151 -- the vast majority of Windows support is confirmed by tests (hardware AMD GL; gpu_mat 4/4, GPU SIFT matching 31/31, opengl_utils 3/3, 1530 assertions pass). The sole GPU-test failure, ExtractSiftFeaturesGPU.Nominal, is a pre-existing upstream COLMAP GL-context-teardown bug in code the port does not modify, filed upstream as https://github.com/colmap/colmap/issues/4633. Not a port defect.

intake.duplicate_effort: none competing; AMD-Ecosystem/colmap fork exists but carries no moat-port/rocm branch -- the only prior work is our own (jeffdaily/colmap: rocm-sift-gpu, rocm-sdk-autodetect, rocm-support*), parked and not yet re-derived onto post-#4420 upstream
intake.summary: BSD-3-Clause (tier 1); dense-reconstruction CUDA->HIP already merged upstream (#4420, our own prior work); remaining gap is GPU SIFT (SiftGPU/ProgramCU.cu, UNC non-commercial vendored licence, contribute-only scope) plus a newly-added, out-of-scope-by-default CASPAR bundle-adjustment CUDA surface (484 generated .cu, Apache-2.0, CASPAR_ENABLED=OFF).

linux-gfx942.blocked_reason: gfx942/MI300X has no HIP image/texture API in ROCm 7.14: the compiler defines __HIP_NO_IMAGE_SUPPORT__ for gfx942, so every tex1Dfetch/tex2D in SiftGPU ProgramCU.cu and in the already-merged MVS kernels (gpu_mat_ref_image.cu, patch_match_cuda.cu, from colmap#4420) fails to compile with 'The image/texture API not supported on the device'; at runtime hipMallocArray and hipCreateTextureObject return hipErrorNotSupported on the device. Pre-existing at head 4c531f5e and independent of this session's fixes. Supporting gfx942 needs a texture-to-buffer rewrite of both the port and the merged MVS code, which is a scope decision for a person. wave64 coverage is already satisfied by gfx90a.
